examples.en: The new employee is really smart.
He handles his work in a smart way.

examples.ko: 스마트한 옷차림이 면접에서 좋은 인상을 줬어요.
examples.en: The sharp outfit made a good impression at the interview.
My younger brother has been smart since he was little.

examples.ko: 스마트하고 친절한 사람과 같이 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work with someone who is smart and kind.
I bought new glasses to look sharp.

explain: '똑똑하다'는 머리가 좋다는 쪽이고, '스마트하다'는 일 처리나 옷차림이 깔끔하고 센스 있다는 쪽에 더 가까워요. 사람뿐 아니라 '스마트한 방법'처럼 방식에도 써요. 공부 머리를 말할 때는 '똑똑하다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: You look sharp in a suit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷차림이나 인상이 깔끔하고 센스 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's outfit or impression looks neat and stylish.

phrases.en: I want to work with a sharp person.
phrases.nuance_ko: '똑똑한 사람'보다 일을 센스 있게 하는 사람이라는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compared with 'smart person', it suggests someone who handles things with good sense.

phrases.en: That method isn't very smart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 방식이 효율적이지 않다고 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft way to say a way of doing things isn't efficient.

explain_en: 똑똑하다 is about brains, while 스마트하다 leans toward being sharp, neat, and savvy, in clothes or in how you get things done. It can also describe methods, as in 스마트한 방법. For academic brightness, Koreans say 똑똑하다 more often.

examples.en: Wearing a light purple dress makes you look bright.
The curtains in my room are a soft light purple.
Light purple flowers bloom a lot in spring.
What colors go well with light purple?

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 친구가 연보라색 우산을 빌려줬어요.
examples.en: On a rainy day, my friend lent me a light purple umbrella.
The sky turned light purple because of the sunset.

explain: '연-'은 색 이름 앞에 붙어 '연한' 느낌을 줘요. 같은 방식으로 '연분홍', '연노랑'도 있어요. 말할 때는 '색'을 빼고 '연보라 원피스'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The light purple bag goes well with the clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '색'을 빼고 짧게 말하는 구어체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short spoken form without 'saek'.

phrases.en: In spring, many light purple flowers bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색 이름 뒤에 명사를 붙여 물건을 꾸며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a noun after the color to describe an object.

phrases.en: I painted the wall light purple.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'를 붙여 어떤 색으로 바꾸거나 고르는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 'euro' you say which color something is made or chosen in.

explain_en: The prefix '연-' before a color name gives a light, pale feel. The same pattern gives '연분홍' (light pink) and '연노랑' (light yellow). In speech you can drop '색' and say '연보라 원피스'.

en: to be interesting; to be fun

examples.en: This drama is really fun.
My grandmother told me old stories in an entertaining way.

examples.ko: 재미난 이야기가 있으면 저한테도 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If you have an interesting story, tell me too.
The movie I saw yesterday was more fun than I expected.

examples.ko: 할머니 이야기는 들을수록 재미나서 시간 가는 줄 몰라요.
examples.en: Grandma's stories get more fun the more I listen, and I lose track of time.
If a book is fun, I read it even if I stay up all night.

explain: '재미있다'와 바꿔 쓸 수 있지만 조금 더 친근하고 이야기하는 느낌이 있어요. '재미난 이야기', '재미나게 놀다'처럼 많이 써요. 반대말은 '재미없다'이고, '재미나지 않다'보다는 '재미없다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: My grandfather told me a fun story.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요. 이야기와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun; it pairs especially well with 'story'.

phrases.en: I had fun playing with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 어떻게 노는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-게' describes how you played.

phrases.en: The movie I saw yesterday was really fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일을 친근하게 이야기할 때 쓰는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used to chat in a friendly way about something earlier.

explain_en: It can replace '재미있다', but it sounds a bit friendlier, like storytelling. It's common in '재미난 이야기' (an interesting story) and '재미나게 놀다' (to play happily). The opposite is '재미없다', which sounds more natural than '재미나지 않다'.

examples.en: I bought a pink bag.
A light pink suits my younger sibling well.

examples.ko: 공원이 벚꽃 때문에 온통 핑크로 보여요.
examples.en: The park looks all pink because of the cherry blossoms.
This pink is so strong that it feels like too much.
I tried wearing pink and white together.
Strawberry milk is cute because it is a pretty pink.

explain: 같은 색을 '분홍색'이라고도 해요. '핑크'는 외래어라 옷·화장품·가게 이름처럼 세련된 느낌을 줄 때 많이 쓰고, 일상에서는 둘 다 자연스러워요. 뒤에 '색'을 붙여 '핑크색'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 두 사람 사이에 핑크빛 기류가 흘러요.
phrases.en: a romantic mood; rosy
phrases.nuance_ko: 분홍색이라는 뜻이 아니라 연애가 시작될 것 같은 설렘이나 밝은 전망을 말해요. '핑크빛 미래'처럼도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not about the color itself: it suggests budding romance or a bright outlook, as in '핑크빛 미래' (a rosy future).

explain_en: The same color is also called '분홍색'. '핑크' is a loanword, common for clothes, cosmetics and shop names where a trendy feel is wanted; both are natural in daily speech. You can add '색' to say '핑크색'.

gh: standard word with the color suffix
short form without the color suffix

p.n: Same meaning; 분홍색 is the standard native-Sino word.

en: to be strong; to be powerful; to be mighty

examples.ko: 우리 형은 힘세서 무거운 짐도 번쩍 들어요.
examples.en: My older brother is strong, so he lifts even heavy loads with ease.

examples.ko: 힘센 사람이 와서 이 상자를 좀 옮겨 주세요.
examples.en: Could a strong person come and move this box?

examples.ko: 아빠는 어릴 때 동네에서 제일 힘세다고 소문났어요.
examples.en: Dad was said to be the strongest in the neighborhood when he was young.
That puppy is really strong even though it is small.
Even with age, Grandpa is still strong.

examples.ko: 저 사람은 겉보기와 달리 별로 힘세지 않아요.
examples.en: Unlike how he looks, that person isn't very strong.

explain: '힘이 세다'를 한 단어로 붙여 쓴 형용사라서, 사람 앞에서는 '힘센 사람'처럼 '힘센'이 돼요. 반대는 '약하다'이고, 몸이 튼튼하다는 말과는 조금 달리 '힘이 강하다'는 데 초점이 있어요.

phrases.en: My father is strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: '힘세다'를 띄어 쓴 형태로, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced-out form of 힘세다, more common in speech.

phrases.en: A strong friend carried the bag for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a person.

phrases.en: Wow, you're really strong!
phrases.nuance_ko: '-네요'를 붙여 새로 알게 된 사실에 놀라거나 감탄할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -네요 expresses surprise or admiration at something you just noticed.

explain_en: It is '힘이 세다' fused into one adjective, so before a noun it becomes '힘센', as in '힘센 사람'. The opposite is '약하다', and it focuses on physical power rather than simply having a healthy body.

examples.ko: 어느 맑은 가을날에 가족과 함께 산에 갔어요.
examples.en: On a clear autumn day, I went to the mountains with my family.
The afternoon sunlight of an autumn day is so warm.

examples.ko: 오늘처럼 시원한 가을날이면 밖에 나가고 싶어요.
examples.en: On a cool autumn day like today, I want to go outside.

examples.ko: 가을날엔 낙엽 밟는 소리가 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: On autumn days, I really like the sound of stepping on fallen leaves.

examples.ko: 비 오는 가을날은 왠지 마음이 쓸쓸해요.
examples.en: A rainy autumn day somehow makes me feel lonely.
I kept the autumn day I spent with friends in photos.

explain: '가을철'이 가을이라는 기간을 말한다면 '가을날'은 가을의 어느 하루와 그날의 분위기를 말해요. 같은 식으로 '봄날, 여름날, 겨울날'도 써요. '어느 가을날'처럼 이야기를 시작할 때 자주 어울려요.

phrases.en: One autumn day, I met an old friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기를 시작할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for opening a story.

phrases.example: 비 오는 가을날에는 따뜻한 차가 생각나요.
phrases.en: On a rainy autumn day, I think of warm tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨를 앞에 붙여 그날의 분위기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the weather before it to set the mood of that day.

phrases.en: On an autumn morning, the air is cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하루 중 때를 뒤에 붙여 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can add a time of day after it.

explain_en: While '가을철' refers to the autumn period, '가을날' refers to a single autumn day and its atmosphere. In the same way you can say '봄날, 여름날, 겨울날'. It works well for starting a story, as in '어느 가을날' (one autumn day).

examples.en: The autumn breeze is blowing, so it's perfect for a walk.
I walked slowly along the river in the autumn breeze.
Leaves fall one by one in the autumn wind.
The autumn breeze is cool, but it gets a bit cold in the evening.
I opened the window and heard the sound of the autumn wind.
I listened to a song as refreshing as an autumn breeze.

explain: 선선하고 시원한 느낌이 먼저 떠올라서 '가을바람이 불다', '선선한 가을바람'처럼 자주 써요. 차갑게 세게 부는 '찬바람'과는 느낌이 달라요. 노래나 글에서는 쓸쓸한 마음을 말할 때도 나와요.

phrases.en: The cool autumn breeze feels nice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시원한 느낌을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for the cool, fresh feeling.

phrases.en: When I open the window, the autumn breeze blows in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 부는 것을 말하는 가장 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say the wind is blowing.

phrases.en: I enjoyed the autumn breeze in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밖에 나가서 바람을 즐긴다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of going outside to enjoy the breeze.
phrases.en_equiv: to get some fresh autumn air

explain_en: It first brings to mind a cool, pleasant feeling, so it is often used as '가을바람이 불다' or '선선한 가을바람'. It feels different from '찬바람' (cold wind), which is harsher. In songs and writing it can also express a lonely mood.

examples.en: I got earrings as a birthday present.
My earring fell off and I searched for it for a long time.
There is a small gem set in the earrings.
The right earring is missing.
I bought both the earrings and the necklace as a set.

examples.ko: 이 귀고리는 가벼워서 오래 해도 편해요.
examples.en: These earrings are light, so they're comfortable even after a long time.

explain: '귀걸이'라고도 하며 일상에서 두 말을 다 써요. 동사는 '귀고리를 하다', '귀고리를 끼다/달다'처럼 말하고, 한 쪽은 '한 짝'이라고 세요. 귀에 하는 장식이니 '목걸이, 팔찌'와 짝으로 외우면 좋아요.

phrases.en: I bought new earrings.
phrases.nuance_ko: '귀고리'와 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 둘 다 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 귀고리; both are used in daily speech.

phrases.en: Today I'm wearing big earrings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장식을 몸에 한다고 할 때 '하다'를 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 하다 is commonly used for wearing accessories.

phrases.en: I lost one earring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둘 중 하나를 셀 때 '짝'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 짝 counts one of a pair.

explain_en: It is also called '귀걸이', and both words are used in daily life. You say '귀고리를 하다' or '귀고리를 끼다/달다', and one earring is counted as '한 짝'. It helps to learn it together with '목걸이' and '팔찌'.

examples.en: Maple leaves turn red in autumn.
I picked up the colored leaves that had fallen on the road.
I pressed a colored leaf between the pages of a book to dry it.
I received maple-leaf-shaped cookies as a gift.
When the wind blew, the colored leaves fell in a shower.
The child made a picture out of colored leaves.

explain: '단풍'은 가을에 색이 변한 잎 전체를 말하고, '단풍잎'은 잎 한 장 한 장을 가리켜요. 나무가 물드는 건 '단풍이 들다'라고 하고, '단풍 구경'을 가요. 발음은 [단풍닙]이에요.

phrases.en: The mountain has turned autumn colors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가을에 잎 색이 변할 때 쓰는 말로, '단풍잎'보다 전체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when leaves change color in autumn, referring to the whole scene.

phrases.en: On the weekend I went to see the autumn leaves with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가을 나들이를 갈 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for autumn outings.

phrases.en: I picked up pretty autumn leaves in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 떨어진 잎 한 장을 집을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for picking up a fallen leaf.
phrases.en_equiv: to pick up an autumn leaf

explain_en: '단풍' refers to the autumn colors as a whole, while '단풍잎' points to the individual leaves. The color change is '단풍이 들다', and people go on '단풍 구경' trips. The pronunciation is [단풍닙].
